newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk army warns Islamists in "life or death" fight.
newsitem.headline: Turk army warns Islamists in "life or death" fight.

text.p: Turkey's powerful armed forces struck out at the ruling Islamists on Tuesday with a top general warning that the military struggle against religious activism was vital to the survival of the secular republic.

"Destroying fundamentalism is of life or death importance," General Kenan Deniz, a top army commander, told a special briefing for journalists designed to lay out the military's position in its struggle with the Islamist-led government.

The general also blasted neighbouring Iran, with whom Erbakan has made a special effort to patch up strained ties, for seeking to undermine Turkey by providing overt support for the separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).

"Iran... is continuing with its efforts to destroy the regime in the Turkish republic," said Deniz, a leader in the security forces' fight with the PKK. "It is known to have directed terrorist actions in Turkey."

The general's tough talk follows weeks of mounting tensions between the armed forces, traditional defenders of Turkey's secularist system, and the government of Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.

On Saturday, Erbakan reluctantly agreed to demands from the army for a series of anti-Islamist measures, but his Islam-based Welfare Party has made it clear it was not prepared to go along with reforms that would close Koranic schools.
Turkey's generals have toppled three civilian governments since 1960, but have been content in recent weeks to only hint at possible intervention this time around.
The ensuing crisis has sent political leaders scrambling to find a new government formula excluding Erbakan. It has also put renewed pressure on Turkish markets.
Istanbul shares were steady at midday. The main market index ended the morning session up 0.83 percent shortly after the general's comments.
The index dropped 1.11 percent on Monday and 4.3 percent last week amid rising political instability and fear of snap elections, brokers said.
Turkish leftist leader Bulent Ecevit was meeting other opposition leaders later on Tuesday for talks on forming an alternative, "Islamist-free" government.

Democratic Left Party (DSP) chief Ecevit opened talks with Mesut Yilmaz, leader of the main opposition Motherland Party. He later meets rival leftist leader Deniz Baykal of the Republican People's Party at 2 p.m. (1100 GMT).
DSP sources said Ecevit, a veteran politician and former prime minister, was also scheduled to hold talks with Democratic Turkey Party leader Husamettin Cindoruk at 3.30 p.m. (1230 GMT).

Erbakan's 10-month-old government with Tansu Ciller's secularist True Path Party (DYP) took a body blow at the weekend when two (DYP) ministers resigned in protest at Erbakan's failure to meet the military demands.
Deputy Prime Minister Ciller has so far stood by Erbakan.
Ciller, a U.S.-educated technocrat who was Turkey's first woman prime minister, says she is better placed to persuade the prime minister to toe the army's line from within the coalition.

Initial secularist moves against Islamist activism were evident on Monday when police said they had closed down more than 20 buildings in two western districts where Islamists were holding illegal Koranic lessons.

Separately, a quasi-military court began hearing a case against the preacher at a mosque in the courtyard of Welfare headquarters where Erbakan and the party leadership often worship, the state-run Anatolian news agency said.
Anatolian said mosque preacher Ali Kucuker faces up to three years in jail if found guilty of spreading hatred in a speech at Friday prayers in February.
